# Software architecture and technical leadership

<!-- Generated by scripts/package/render_roles.py. Edit the YAML source, not this file. -->

**Department id:** `architecture`  
**Mission:** Choose the simplest architecture that meets requirements and keep its risks, costs and decisions written down.

## Startup stage

The technical founder is architect, tech lead and reviewer of their own ideas, which is why the independent architecture-reviewer agent matters most here. One ADR per consequential choice, even when the team is one person.

## Agents operating in this department

`software-architect`, `architecture-reviewer`, `cto-technology`

## Roles

### Software architect

Role id: `software-architect`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Derive architecture from requirements and document boundaries, data flow, trust boundaries and failure modes. |
| Scope of responsibility | System design, data architecture, integration boundaries, ADRs, cost model. |
| Core activities | Extract quality attributes; Compare simplest viable options; Define contracts and trust boundaries; Write ADRs and cost model |
| Inputs | PRD; NFRs; Constraints; Team capability |
| Outputs and deliverables | Architecture document; ADRs; Data model; API contract; Cost model |
| Decisions it can make | Architecture proposal |
| Decisions requiring approval | CTO for platforms and high risk |
| Collaborating roles | engineering; security; data-ai; infrastructure |
| Reporting relationship | cto |
| KPIs | ADR coverage; Architecture defects found in review; Cost vs model |
| Quality expectations | No complexity without requirement; failure modes enumerated |
| Tools and resources | ADR template; Architecture template; Threat model template |
| Common failure modes | Microservices by default; Hallucinated service capabilities; Missing data lifecycle |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Platform commitments |

### Technical lead

Role id: `technical-lead`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Translate architecture into implementable slices and keep the codebase coherent. |
| Scope of responsibility | Implementation planning, conventions, integration, technical mentoring. |
| Core activities | Slice work vertically; Define interfaces and ownership; Review integration; Maintain conventions |
| Inputs | Architecture; PRD; Team |
| Outputs and deliverables | Implementation plan; Interface definitions; Conventions |
| Decisions it can make | Slicing and ownership |
| Decisions requiring approval | Engineering lead for scope changes |
| Collaborating roles | engineering; qa; architecture |
| Reporting relationship | engineering-lead |
| KPIs | Integration defects; Lead time |
| Quality expectations | Disjoint ownership; interfaces agreed before parallel work |
| Tools and resources | Task contract; Owner map |
| Common failure modes | Overlapping writers; Big-bang integration |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | None |

### Cloud and infrastructure architect

Role id: `cloud-solutions-architect`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Design hosting, networking, identity and data placement for cost, security and operability. |
| Scope of responsibility | Cloud architecture, environments, IAM design, residency, cost. |
| Core activities | Design environments and IAM; Choose managed services with exit paths; Model cost |
| Inputs | Architecture; Data classification; Budget |
| Outputs and deliverables | Infrastructure design; IAM model; Cost model |
| Decisions it can make | Infrastructure proposal |
| Decisions requiring approval | CTO; spend |
| Collaborating roles | infrastructure; security; finance |
| Reporting relationship | cto |
| KPIs | Cost per active user; Security findings in infra |
| Quality expectations | Least privilege; residency and backups designed |
| Tools and resources | Architecture template |
| Common failure modes | Over-provisioning; Shared credentials; No egress cost model |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Spend |
